title.narrative: Response to the socioeconomic impact of COVID 19 and effects of climate change on livehoods and food security in the Gulf of Fonseca Region (R13)

description.narrative: El objetivo general de la acción es apoyar a los hogares vulnerables afectados por el impacto del COVID-19 y el cambio climático, en particular a los productores y jornaleros en la región del Golfo de Fonseca a través de la asistencia alimentaria, fortaleciendo los medios de vida resilientes a través de la diversificación y la adaptación de procesos, (incluyendo gestión de riesgos, equidad de género y capacitación en nutrición) y, mejorar la gobernanza local y sus capacidades

title.narrative: Food Expenditure Share

description.narrative: This indicator measures the proportion of each households available budget (estimated through an expenditure module) spent on food. It is important that the overall budget/expenses does not only consider cash expenses but also purchases made on credit, items produced by the household (e.g. own production) and assistance received.

comment.narrative: 88 of households use 50100 of their income to maintain their food consumption. This indicator places 50.45 of the population in severe insecurity at 37.84 in moderate and marginal insecurity. Households are more vulnerable to any kind of crisis when they must invest most of their income in food because households do not have enough income to respond to other major household expenses such as health education wellbeing and other unforeseen events. On the other hand at least 54.1 of households are in debt. This indebtedness is attributed to the purchase of food which has been required of the Pulpero rural box lender friendships and others.
70 of households spending 50 or more decreased

title.narrative: Consumptionbased Coping Strategy Index, reduced CSI (rCSI)

description.narrative: The Reduced Coping Strategy Index (rCSI), also called CSI food, is used to assess the level of stress3 faced by a household due to a food shortage. It is measured by combining the frequency and severity of the food consumptionbased strategies households are engaging in. It is calculated using the five standard4 strategies using a 7day recall period. Description of five consumptionbased coping strategies Coping Strategies:1. Rely on less preferred and less expensive food2. Borrow food or rely on help from relative(s) or friend(s)3. Limit portion size at meals4. Restrict consumption by adults for small children to eat5. Reduce number of meals eaten in a day

comment.narrative: More than 40 of households report the adoption of 4 foodrelated coping mechanisms such as rely on less preferred and expensive foods 82 limit portion sizes in meals 67.6 reduce the number of meals eaten in a day 59.6 borrowed food or rely on help from family or friends 41.1.
Reduced 80 rCSI compared to preassistance baseline value.

title.narrative: Livelihood Coping Strategies Indicator

description.narrative: The livelihoodsbased coping strategies module is used to better understand longerterm coping capacity of households. For each country, the module must be adapted to suit each countrys context and poor peoples living conditions. This requires the selection of relevant coping strategies from the coping strategies master list (see Table 1 below). Each strategy is associated with a level of severity (none, stress, crisis or emergency), which is country or contextspecific. The module must include four stress strategies, three crisis strategies and three emergency strategies (ten strategies in total). Stress strategies indicate a reduced ability to deal with future shocks as the result of a current reduction in resources or increase in debts. Crisis strategies are often associated with the direct reduction of future productivity. Emergency strategies also affect future productivity, but are more difficult to reverse or more dramatic in nature than crisis strategies.The module collects additional information about households who did not employ a particular livelihoodcoping strategy. In this case, the respondent is asked why they did not apply it (no need, or because they had already exhausted the strategy).

For each country, the module must be adapted to suit each countrys context and poor peoples living conditions. Each strategy is associated with a level of severity (none, stress, crisis or emergency), which is country or contextspecific. The module must include four stress strategies, three crisis strategies and three emergency strategies (ten strategies in total). Stress strategies indicate a reduced ability to deal with future shocks as the result of a current reduction in resources or increase in debts. Crisis strategies are often associated with the direct reduction of future productivity. Emergency strategies also affect future productivity, but are more difficult to reverse or more dramatic in nature than crisis strategies.The module collects additional information about households who did not employ a particular livelihoodcoping strategy. In this case, the respondent is asked why they did not apply it (no need, or because they had already exhausted the strategy).
